name: Baptism
reason: Source term 'Baptism of the Laws' (also rendered 'Law Baptism') was localized as 'Baptism by Laws', a near-literal rendering that fits the Western fantasy register.
description: The Baptism by Laws is an extremely rare transformative phenomenon in the upper world, triggered at the ancient law obelisks engraved by master cultivators from the age of the ancient dragons. It rewrites a cultivator's potential and renders them compatible with all law refinement; the previous recorded occurrence was eight thousand four hundred years before Zane's. During his Baptism by Laws, Zane mastered all nine original laws, a feat so extraordinary that even mentioning it would invite disbelief.

name: Dragonfall Palace
issues: Source translation alternates between 'Dragon Abyss Palace' and 'Dragon Pool Palace' for the same organization; the adaptation correctly unified both under 'Dragonfall Palace'.
reason: The source organization 'Dragon Abyss Palace' (also translated 'Dragon Pool Palace') was renamed 'Dragonfall Palace', keeping the dragon motif in a more dramatic Western fantasy register.
description: Dragonfall Palace is a powerful upper-world organization run by the Dragon-blooded, counterpart to Dragonblaze Hall. Its head offered Zane a drop of the True Dragon's Heartblood, one of the Palace's most sacred treasures, and Zane belongs to it as a dragon-blood, though he initially declined to join right away. It issues standard Relic-Class equipment, including the armor Zane later gifted to Tia.

name: Red Cloud Ring
reason: The source artifact 'Scarlet Dawn Ring' (also rendered 'Crimson Ring') was localized as 'Red Cloud Ring' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: The Red Cloud Ring is a giant glowing hoop used as a screening device before warriors may enter Passing the Torch: flying through it lets it sense their strength and estimate how many lotus petals they have activated. It is only calibrated to register a Lesser Lotus Flower, and anything more powerful simply overloads it; fewer than ten percent of candidates made it through. Layla oversaw the testing from above the ring.

name: Julius
reason: The source character is known only by his title, the 'Hua Tian City Lord'; the adaptation gave him the personal name 'Julius', an imposing classical name fitting an arrogant city ruler.
description: Julius is the arrogant lord of an upper-world city who wields blood-based powers, shaping a longspear from a swirling vortex of boiling blood and traveling in a blood-mist form. He dismisses Zane as a fool overestimating his own strength, tries to use a captive woman as a bargaining chip, and has his physical body destroyed in their fight, after which he leads Sloan to hunt Zane down for his treasures.

name: Celestial Mice
reason: The source beast species 'Heaven Reaching Rats' was localized as 'Celestial Mice', keeping the heavenly connotation in a cleaner English form.
description: Celestial Mice are a legendary beast species ranked number one among their kind, said to be second only to the greater legendary beasts themselves, with an insane rate of reproduction. In the Illusion Battlefield arc, Zane fights three of them guarding a cave; they refuse to give up even when charred black, and reportedly 'respawn' after a period of time.

name: Five Elements
reason: The classical source concept 'Five Elements' was kept as-is, since the term already reads naturally in a Western fantasy register.
description: The Five Elements are the five fundamental powers whose balanced fusion underlies an unbelievably powerful martial art, 'The Godly Way of the Five Elements' (the source's Five Elements Divine Dao). Their combined power is the same principle behind the Lodestone, and objects infused with them glow with many colors and radiate their aura; wielding the Godly Way burns through vitality at a terrifying rate.

name: World’s Will
reason: The source concept 'Will of the World' was localized near-literally as the 'World's Will' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: The World's Will is the consciousness of the world itself, which Zane secretly merged with, granting him a state of near-omniscience. Its Memory holds a record of every living being in the world, past and present, and Zane frequently consults the Memory of the World's Will to investigate people and events; a complete blank in that record marks something deeply abnormal.

name: Celestial Tribulation
reason: The source term 'Heavenly Tribulation' (Heavenly Dao Tribulation) was localized as 'Celestial Tribulation' to fit the adaptation's Western fantasy register.
description: The Celestial Tribulation is a disaster sent from the heavens to strike down warriors at breakthrough, descending in successive waves and embodied in a lightning dragon that serves no master. A lesser Celestial Tribulation strikes the moment a Life-and-Death Realm warrior appears, and Zane eventually learns not merely to survive the tribulation but to harness it as a weapon.

name: Hobbes
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Yan Yueshan' was fully localized to 'Hobbes', a blunt, forceful Western name fitting his fierce, hot-tempered strongman archetype.
description: Hobbes is one of the three leaders of the World Merchants' Guild Alliance alongside Kieran and Burns, a Spirit-Tribulation Realm authority figure with a sun-darkened, fierce appearance. He is hot-tempered, impatient, and famous for his explosive strength, though even his body alone could not shatter the barrier the trio faced; in the source he is Yan Yueshan, the fierce-looking member of the three alliance masters.

name: Primordial Energy
reason: The source's 'Primordial Astral Nova' (the primordial power accumulated in Luo Zheng's body, tempered by the Primordial Astral Winds) was simplified to 'Primordial Energy' for clarity in audio.
description: Primordial Energy is the fundamental power stored within Zane's own body, revealed when the dragon began refining his body with its own Primordial Energy, declaring his body a vessel of it. Distinct from Vitality, it had previously been mistaken for purging energy, and the seventh brother taught Zane how to summon and circulate it for Body Refining.

name: Gate
reason: The source describes an unnamed, lonely free-standing door left behind by Qing Yuanzi; the adaptation capitalized it as 'the Gate' to give the artifact a proper identity.
description: The Gate is a mysterious free-standing door discovered in the Mysterious Underworld Cave arc, reached only after an exhausting journey. Passing through it subjects a warrior to successive trials with a maximum of ninety-nine, a limit Zane reaches, and its true gift is a breakthrough to the War Sage level (the source's War Saint realm).

name: Kensington
reason: The source's 'Xi Family' aristocratic clan was localized as house 'Kensington', an upscale British-flavored surname conveying old nobility.
description: Kensington is one of the seven influential third-grade houses in Ethereal City, alongside Langley, Hawthorne, Chambers, Sutton, Shaw, and Carter, wealthy enough to line its estate walls with Aether Crystal lanterns. The house is best known for its daughter (the source's Xi Youqin), a picky young lady of higher status than a princess whom no suitor has managed to impress, and whom Zane escorts into the marshes.

name: Lord Randy
issues: Name reuse: a different, unrelated minor character 'Randy' (Duskfall Sect disciple, killed by a Nether Phantom in Ep 386) already existed in Eps 383-386; 'Lord Randy' (Eps 786-875) is a separate character and should not be merged with him.
reason: The source character, known by the royal title 'King of Yan' (Yan Wang), was localized as 'Lord Randy', trading the Chinese kingdom title for a Western lordship.
description: Lord Randy is a sharp, venomous noble of the Second Tier encountered in the Martial House arc, considered a peer of the man from the Divine Kingdom and far beyond most challengers. He keeps his gaze locked threateningly on Zane, consorts with Master Hill, and takes crazed pleasure in tormenting his own wife, marking him as one of the arc's cruelest antagonists.

name: Ancestral Dragon Egg
reason: The source term 'Ancestral Dragon' egg was kept near-literally as 'Ancestral Dragon Egg', since the name already suits the Western fantasy register.
description: The Ancestral Dragon Egg is a legendary egg waiting in the Sacred Feather Sea, holding the secrets of the dragon-blooded, with something alive moving inside it. It lies wrapped in chains and sealed within another layer of space, and powerful figures such as Dorothea fear disaster should anyone interfere with its hatching; the key to it is held in a treasure more important than three others combined.

name: Liam Shaw
issues: Name drift: early delivered episodes (Eps 1-100 batch) originally used 'Declan' for this character; 'Liam Shaw' is canonical per the master sheet and delivered episodes.
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Cao Lei' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Liam' was chosen as a smooth, contemporary name masking his cunning nature, with the surname 'Shaw' tying him to an established house.
description: Liam Shaw is a cunning schemer from the Dragon's Keep (source: Dragon Castle) arc who plots against Zane while keeping up a reasonable front, hardening his tone when words fail and toasting allies like Randall, a Nature Level fighter from Dragon's Keep. His true colors show when he attacks with a hidden golden needle launched from a concealed mechanism, matching the source character Cao Lei's treacherous strike.

name: Demonic Grunt
reason: The source term 'Demon Soldier' was localized as 'Demonic Grunt', emphasizing their status as fodder-level troops in the demon army.
description: Demonic Grunts are the lowest, fodder-level tier of the demon army encountered in the sect-defense arc. They fight in ranks under generals and commanders, savage enough to bite the head off a disciple, but they break rank and flee for their lives at the sight of their general's horrific end.

name: Maiden's Peak
reason: The source location 'Jade Maiden Peak' was localized as 'Maiden's Peak', dropping the Chinese 'Jade' modifier for a cleaner Western name.
description: Maiden's Peak is the sect division reserved exclusively for female cultivators, the subject of its own legend among disciples. Since Elara's arrival it transformed into a formidable powerhouse within the Sect, and through her efforts alone it secured a second-place finish in the sect competition.

name: Heavy Water
reason: The source term 'heavy water' was kept as-is, since the literal term already works in the Western fantasy setting.
description: Heavy Water is the viscous, surprisingly clear water filling the depths of the diving-trial pool (the source's Illusory Fish Deep Pool), roughly ten times heavier than ordinary water with astonishing buoyancy and crushing pressure. Zane learns to stop resisting it and let its hidden currents shoot him forward with startling velocity while Leo and the steward assume he has given up.

name: Bloody Mountain
reason: The source location 'Blood Red Mountain' was localized as 'Bloody Mountain', a tighter name for the trial ground in the Western fantasy register.
description: Bloody Mountain is the trial ground for The Gauntlet, divided into five zones, which Great House disciples ascend ahead of the thousand ordinary disciples while mentors watch from outside. It is the site of Zane's early trial, where Joe Fane used his Spirit Weapon to create unbreakable energy wire, and its delicate, intricate arrays remain a point of comparison long afterward.

name: House Warrick
reason: The source's landowning 'Wang Family' was localized as 'House Warrick', a strong Anglo-Norman house name fitting a prominent Legacy House.
description: House Warrick is the Legacy House of Adrian and Caleb, an enormous family with countless side branches, prominent but still several rungs below the Capital's elite circles. Zane's early defiance of Caleb broke a dam of resentment against the house's arrogance, and his later feud with Lennon pits him against the combined House Warrick and House Anderson.

name: Crimson Sect
reason: The source's 'Drifting Cloud Sect' was renamed the 'Crimson Sect' to match the adaptation's crimson-robed visual identity and avoid yet another 'Cloud' sect name.
description: The Crimson Sect is a Grade Two sect under the Cloud Hall, based in the resource-rich Heartlands and stronger than the Skyreach Sect. Its leader Eddy Warrick (source: Wei Yulong) arrives with nine beginning Soul Realm disciples who wear crimson robes, mock Zane's talent, and are stunned that someone at Grade Three of the Adept Realm could touch the Spatial Laws; their home competition is The Crimson Crucible.

name: Bloodwood Cliff
reason: The source sect 'Blood Wood Cliff' was kept near-literally as 'Bloodwood Cliff', compounding the name for smoother English.
description: Bloodwood Cliff is a fourth-grade sect led by Lady Darkmere, known for dark arts and forbidden techniques such as the Soul-Killing Poisoned Blood. It stands alongside the Cloud Hall, the Black Mountain Sect, and the Ethereal Spirit Sect in guarding major events, and its arrogant disciples sneer at Soul Realm challengers like Zane, fielding fighters such as Brody Booth against him.

name: Troy
reason: The source character 'Old Wu', a brash soldier, was localized as 'Troy', a punchy single name suiting a cocky sparring-circle bruiser.
description: Troy is a cocky fighter from the Dragon's Keep arc who plants himself in the sparring circle and beckons Zane out, caring nothing for his reputation. He loads everything into a single swing, only for Zane, a kid at the Marrow Refining Level, to catch his fist with one hand, leaving Troy flushed beet red in front of everyone.

name: Spirit Supreme
reason: The source cultivation stage 'Divine Extreme Realm' was renamed 'Spirit Supreme' to fit the adaptation's realm ladder (Soul Sea, Spirit Supreme, Spirit Transformation, World Lords).
description: Spirit Supreme is a high cultivation realm sitting above the Soul Sea Realm and below the Spirit Transformation Realm, the stages separating Soul Sea cultivators from the colossal gap up to World Lords. Spirit Supreme masters wield power beyond ordinary comprehension, and sensing even a dozen of them in a crowd marks an elite gathering; in the source these are the Divine Extreme Realm powerhouses of the Three Transformations.

name: Sloan
reason: The source character 'Hall Master Shen' was localized as 'Sloan', a sleek surname-style name echoing 'Shen' and fitting his smooth, powerful persona.
description: Sloan is a silk-voiced power broker of the upper world (the source's Hall Master Shen, who controls a thousand cities through the Xu Hua Palace). Summoned by Julius after Zane destroys the city lord's body, he follows Julius's blood-mist form across the city, recognizes something familiar in Zane, and suspects from the beginning that the young man has powerful connections.

name: Psychean Realm
reason: The source's 'Psychic World', one of the universe's large worlds, was localized as the 'Psychean Realm', a coined adjectival form with a more mythic ring.
description: The Psychean Realm is the large world that is home to the Soulbound Sect, whose Saint Lord is a figure most of its warriors could barely look up to. Even Fenton, who seemed untouchable to most Soulbound Sect warriors, ranked only third there, and Zane's party is formally welcomed into the realm before later departing it by ship.

name: Dark Law
reason: The source term 'Law of Darkness' was localized as 'Dark Law', a tighter form consistent with the adaptation's other law names.
description: The Dark Law is an extremely rare law power that acts as the nemesis of light, able to devour illumination entirely and weave darkness into an impenetrable curtain that shields whoever hides inside. Zane senses it radiating from illusion-cloaked moths and from the oppressive blackness at the underground palace, though his special sight lets him see through some of its illusions.

name: Addison
issues: Ep 1182's phrasing ('the Queen of Punishment, Addison, and her opponent, Gunter') reads as if Addison were the female Queen of Punishment, but all other episodes use male pronouns for him, matching the male source character Empyrean Darkdemon; the Ep 1182 apposition should be treated as a list of separate characters.
reason: The source character 'Empyrean Darkdemon' (Old Monster Darkdemon of the demon race) was localized as 'Addison', a modern Western name assigned to the Ogre Supreme Lord.
description: Addison is the Ogre Supreme Lord, renowned as one of the oldest and most powerful beings in the universe, whose mere presence through the Keep's walls quickens Zane's heart. First to arrive in the hunt for the Crown, he trails black smoke when he acts, roars in frustrated shock when outmaneuvered, and lunges with the other Supreme Lords for the miniature Elysian Keep.
